title: Equivalence operations on relative universal cones
statement:
Use quasicategories, functor equivalences, coherent transformations and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the relative universal diagrams of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], using its path-pullback model for strictly commuting squares of Kan complexes. The quasicategory and Kan-mapping-space assertions needed for these squares are supplied by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Inner fibrations have the meaning of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]; an isofibration between quasicategories is an inner fibration lifting equivalence edges with any specified source over the source of the given edge. All objects are small in a fixed sufficiently large universe. The following equivalence operations preserve relative universal diagrams.
(1) Let $M$ be any small simplicial set. If $p:D\to B$ is a functor of quasicategories and $q,q':M^{\triangleright}\to D$ are naturally equivalent as coherent diagrams, then $q$ is a $p$-colimit diagram if and only if $q'$ is.
(2) Let $p:D\to B$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories, $e:L\to M$ an equivalence of quasicategories, $f:M\to D$ and $g:M^{\triangleright}\to B$ satisfy $pf=g|_M$. The existence of a $p$-colimit diagram $q:M^{\triangleright}\to D$ with $q|_M=f$ and $pq=g$ is equivalent to the existence of one on $L^{\triangleright}$ with boundary $fe$ and base $ge^{\triangleright}$. For any particular $q:M^{\triangleright}\to D$, it is a $p$-colimit diagram if and only if $qe^{\triangleright}$ is one.
(3) If $p:D\to B$ is an inner fibration of quasicategories, $M$ a quasicategory with final object $t$, and $q:M^{\triangleright}\to D$ a $p$-colimit diagram, then its edge $a:q(t)\to q(*)$ is $p$-cocartesian. Here $p$-cocartesian has the horn-lifting meaning of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. If $p(a)$ is an equivalence, then $a$ is an equivalence.
(4) Define the opposite simplicial set by precomposition with order reversal on the simplex category: an operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ is replaced by $j\mapsto n-\alpha(m-j)$. Opposites of quasicategories are quasicategories; opposites of isofibrations are isofibrations. For every quasicategory $D$ and vertices $x,y$, there are natural equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{D^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_D(y,x)$. For a small simplicial set $M$ and a functor $p:D\to B$ of quasicategories, under $(M^{\triangleleft})^{\mathrm{op}}\cong(M^{\mathrm{op}})^{\triangleright}$, a diagram $q:M^{\triangleleft}\to D$ is a $p$-limit diagram if and only if $q^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a $p^{\mathrm{op}}$-colimit diagram. For any quasicategory $C$ and vertex $c$, the opposite of $C_{c/}$ is canonically $(C^{\mathrm{op}})_{/c}$, respecting the entire remaining face and the canonical cone/cocone. The corresponding duals of (1)-(3) hold.

proof.text: We will use the following immediate consequence of [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance]: a strictly commuting cube of squares of Kan complexes whose four comparison maps are weak equivalences preserves and reflects being a homotopy pullback. Indeed the induced map between their three-corner path pullbacks is a weak equivalence by that node; the two comparison maps from the upper-left corners commute with it, so two-out-of-three gives the assertion. For homotopy-commuting square presentations we use the same argument on the specified path data: a comparison sends $(u,v,\gamma)$ to the two compared endpoints and the path formed by its first commutation homotopy, the image of $\gamma$, and its second commutation homotopy in reverse. A weak equivalence of Kan complexes has a homotopy inverse here: [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance], applied with each endpoint as the Kan target, makes precomposition bijective on homotopy classes; first lift the identity of the source to get $vu\simeq1$, then use injectivity with the other target to get $uv\simeq1$. Applying inverse comparisons to the path triples gives inverse maps up to homotopy, since the commutation paths cancel with their reverses, and the specified cube coherence identifies the endpoint homotopies. This also proves preservation of the comparison from the fourth corner, so two-out-of-three applies to homotopy-commuting square presentations. This applies to the testing squares in [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. To prove (1) without choosing incompatible inverses of their corners, put $J=N(\{0\cong1\})$ as in [lem-coef-quasicategory-invertible-interval]. The natural equivalence between $q$ and $q'$ extends to a map $J\to\operatorname{Fun}(M^{\triangleright},D)$ by that node, since these two objects are isomorphic in the category generated by edges and triangle relations. Currying gives $w:M^{\triangleright}\to\operatorname{Fun}(J,D)$ with endpoints exactly $q,q'$. Put $p_J=\operatorname{Fun}(J,p)$. For either endpoint $\epsilon$, evaluation on $\operatorname{Fun}(T,\operatorname{Fun}(J,D))\cong\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Fun}(T,D))$ is a trivial Kan fibration, again by the invertible-interval node, for $T=M$ and $T=M^{\triangleright}$, and likewise with $B$. A trivial Kan fibration lifts all monomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms]; hence it is a trivial Joyal fibration by the cofibration/trivial-fibration weak factorization system in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. The characterization in [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] makes it a functor equivalence. Its maps on all mapping spaces are consequently equivalences by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Evaluation therefore gives precisely such a strict cube between the square for $(w,t)$ and the square for $(q_\epsilon,\operatorname{ev}_\epsilon t)$. If $q_\epsilon$ is universal, every $t$ passes the square test for $w$. Conversely, every test diagram $t_0$ for $q_\epsilon$ is the evaluation of the diagram constant in the $J$ variable with value $t_0$, so universality of $w$ implies that of $q_\epsilon$. Thus $q$ is a $p$-colimit if and only if $w$ is a $p_J$-colimit if and only if $q'$ is a $p$-colimit. No fibration condition on $p$ or quasicategory condition on $M$ was used.

proof.text: For the particular-diagram assertion of (2), choose a quasi-inverse $d:M\to L$ of $e$. Precomposition gives quasi-inverse functors $e^*:\operatorname{Fun}(M,D)\to\operatorname{Fun}(L,D)$ and $d^*$: whiskering the two inverse-equivalence witnesses gives their inverse witnesses, which are equivalences by the componentwise criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The same holds with $B$. Thus restriction induces equivalences on the two spaces of cocones with constant target, by the mapping-space assertion of that node. The constant-target criterion [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] compares $q$ and $qe^{\triangleright}$ using squares with the same left corners $\operatorname{Map}_D(q(*),z)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_B(pq(*),pz)$, and these two equivalences as right-corner maps. Its restriction-naturality clause identifies the maps: both send $u$ to the original cocone restricted along $e$, followed by $\Delta(u)$. The square comparison, with its specified composition homotopies, therefore preserves and reflects the path-pullback condition by the strict-cube argument of step 1, or its natural path-model presentation. This proves $q$ universal if and only if $qe^{\triangleright}$ universal. This part in fact needs no fibration hypothesis on $p$.

source.place: Corollary 7.2.2.2 (02XQ), specialized to an indexing equivalence, proved by the constant-target form of Proposition 7.1.6.19 (02X1); online sources read, archive WANTED; explicit agent argument.

proof.text:
Here is the anodyne restriction fact needed for strict existence. Let $i:A\hookrightarrow N$ be right anodyne and let $Q:N^{\triangleright}\to D$ be any diagram. The cocone-mapping-space clause of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] says that, for each $z$, restriction gives an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N,D)}(Q|_N,\Delta_Nz)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,D)}(Qi,\Delta_Az),$$
and gives the same result for $pQ$ in $B$, compatibly with postcomposition by arrows out of the apex. Consequently the two right corners of the constant-target square are equivalences and the two left corners are identities. The restriction compatibility in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] and the path-pullback invariance of [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] show that $Q$ is a $p$-colimit if and only if $Qi^{\triangleright}$ is. This works for arbitrary simplicial indices and does not assert that restriction on whole functor categories along $i$ is an equivalence.

source.place: Corollary 7.2.2.2 (02XQ), right-anodyne case via constant targets; online sources read, archive WANTED; explicit agent argument.

proof.text:
Now suppose a $p$-colimit $q_L$ with the boundary and base in (2) is given. Factor $e=ri$ as $L\xrightarrow{i}N\xrightarrow{r}M$ by [lem-coef-infinity-equivalence-anodyne-factorization]. Prescribe $fr$ on $N$ and $q_L$ on $L^{\triangleright}$; these agree on $L$ because $ri=e$. Their common prescribed base is $gr^{\triangleright}$. The pushout-join assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones], applied to $i$ and $\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$, makes
$$N\amalg_L L^{\triangleright}\hookrightarrow N^{\triangleright}$$
inner anodyne. The lifting property of the inner fibration $p$ in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] extends the prescribed map to $Q:N^{\triangleright}\to D$ over $gr^{\triangleright}$, exactly: lift each inner-horn attachment, use the union of the compatible maps at a limit ordinal, and restrict a lift for an arrow of which this one is a retract. Step 3 makes $Q$ universal. The trivial Kan fibration $r$ has a section $s:M\to N$ by [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence]. By [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] and the two Joyal nodes, $r$ is a functor equivalence (the same weak-factorization-system argument as in step 1). Since $rs=1_M$, two-out-of-three in the Joyal model structure and its characterization between quasicategories make $s$ a functor equivalence too. Step 2 then makes $q=Qs^{\triangleright}$ universal, and
$$q|_M=frs=f,\qquad pq=gr^{\triangleright}s^{\triangleright}=g$$
are equalities of simplicial maps. Conversely an existing $q$ on $M^{\triangleright}$ restricts along $e^{\triangleright}$, with exactly the stated boundary and base, and is universal by step 2. This proves the existence equivalence, without replacing any prescribed map by an equivalent one.

source.place: Proposition 7.2.2.9 (02XT), right-anodyne/trivial-Kan factorization argument; online sources read, archive WANTED; explicit agent argument.

proof.text: For (3), [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-anodyne] makes $\{t\}\hookrightarrow M$ right anodyne. Step 3 restricts $q$ to a $p$-colimit diagram on $\{t\}^{\triangleright}=\Delta^1$, namely $a:q(t)\to q(*)$. In the apex criterion [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] for this one-point index, $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,D)=D$, its induced coherent cocone is just $a$, and the square is precisely the precomposition square of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. That node applies because $p$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories, so $a$ is horn-cocartesian. If $p(a)$ is an equivalence, its inverse and the associativity/unit homotopies in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] make precomposition by $p(a)$ a homotopy equivalence on every mapping space. A homotopy pullback of this equivalence is an equivalence, by [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] applied to the span and its span with that corner replaced by its equivalent target. For completeness, write the latter span as $u:U\to W\leftarrow W:1_W$. Its path pullback consists of $(b,w,\gamma)$ with $\gamma(0)=u(b)$ and $\gamma(1)=w$. The projection to $b\in U$ has section $b\mapsto(b,u(b),\operatorname{const}_{u(b)})$. The simplicial homotopy $H_t(b,w,\gamma)=(b,\gamma(t),s\mapsto\gamma(\min(s,t)))$ joins section followed by projection at $t=0$ to the identity at $t=1$; its starting point stays $u(b)$, and its ending point is the displayed new second coordinate. It is simplicial because $\min:\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^1$ is monotone. Thus precomposition by $a$ induces bijections on components $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_D(q(*),z)\to\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_D(q(t),z)$ for every $z$. At $z=q(t)$ obtain $b:q(*)\to q(t)$ with $[b][a]=1$; at $z=q(*)$, injectivity gives $[a][b]=1$ since both sides become $[a]$ after composition with $[a]$. The last criterion in the mapping-composition node supplies the two inverse-triangle witnesses, so $a$ is an equivalence.

source.place: Corollary 7.2.2.5 (02XV) and Proposition 5.1.1.9 (01TB), with the equivalence implication expanded on mapping spaces; online sources read, archive WANTED; explicit agent argument.

proof.text:
Write $\rho_n(a)=n-a$. The operator formula in (4) is $\alpha\mapsto\rho_n\alpha\rho_m$; it preserves composition and squares to the identity. It takes the $i$th horn in dimension $n$ to the $(n-i)$th horn. Hence inner horns remain inner, all horns remain horns, and opposites preserve quasicategories, inner fibrations and Kan complexes directly from their lifting definitions. Reversing the two ordered join blocks gives $(X\star Y)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong Y^{\mathrm{op}}\star X^{\mathrm{op}}$, including the degree $-1$ pure-factor cases in [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. In the coslice, an $n$-simplex is a map $\Delta^{n+1}\to C$ with first vertex $c$. Reversal sends it to a simplex of $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ with last vertex $c$, and the remaining face is reversed with all its operators. This is exactly the canonical isomorphism $(C_{c/})^{\mathrm{op}}\cong(C^{\mathrm{op}})_{/c}$, and it respects the associated whole cone, not just its objects. Finally, reversing a product simplex gives
$$(\operatorname{Fun}(K,D))^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},D^{\mathrm{op}}).$$
In degree $n$ this sends a map $K\times\Delta^n\to D$ to its opposite, using $(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\Delta^n$; the displayed operator formula verifies naturality. Reversing the two inverse triangles for an equivalence reverses the equivalence, so this also preserves equivalence components.

source.place: Definition 7.1.6.1 (02KG), Remark 7.1.6.2; elementary order-reversal and join/slice formulas; online sources read, archive WANTED; explicit agent argument.

proof.text:
We check the mapping-space convention rather than identifying the two pinch models. For a simplicial set $T$, subdivision as in [lem-coef-subdivision-face-poset-calculus] has a natural isomorphism $\operatorname{Sd}T\cong\operatorname{Sd}(T^{\mathrm{op}})$: on the summand of a simplex $\sigma:\Delta^n\to T$, send a flag of nonempty subsets $(S_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S_k)$ to $(\rho_nS_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\rho_nS_k)$ in the reversed simplex. For a monotone $\alpha$, $\rho_n\alpha=(\rho_n\alpha\rho_m)\rho_m$, so this respects the colimit identifications and is involutive. The last-vertex maps on both sides are weak equivalences by [lem-coef-subdivision-last-vertex-equivalence]. This gives a natural zigzag $T\leftarrow\operatorname{Sd}T\cong\operatorname{Sd}(T^{\mathrm{op}})\to T^{\mathrm{op}}$. Independently, $[\sigma,(t_0,\ldots,t_n)]\mapsto[\sigma,(t_n,\ldots,t_0)]$ is a natural homeomorphism $|T^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|T|$: the same conjugation formula respects precisely the realization relations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the map and its inverse descend from continuous maps on each simplex. Thus reversal preserves and reflects weak homotopy equivalences.
For the Kan arrow spaces of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], reversing the parameter simplex and interchanging the two endpoints gives a strict natural isomorphism
$$U_{D^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,y)\cong U_D(y,x)^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
Combine this isomorphism, the natural subdivision zigzag for $U_D(y,x)$, and the two natural pinch equivalences to obtain the required natural equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{D^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_D(y,x)$. To use these zigzags in the Kan path-pullback model, apply [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products] to the subdivision zigzag. Its functor $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}$ sends every simplicial set to a Kan complex and its natural unit is a weak equivalence. It preserves weak equivalences by two-out-of-three applied to the natural unit square. Thus replace the span $T\leftarrow\operatorname{Sd}T\to T^{\mathrm{op}}$ by the all-Kan zigzag $T\to\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}T\leftarrow\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}\operatorname{Sd}T\to\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}(T^{\mathrm{op}})\leftarrow T^{\mathrm{op}}$ when $T$ is Kan, incorporating the subdivision isomorphism in the middle arrow. Every arrow is a weak equivalence, and the construction is natural. These are natural zigzags of Kan complexes, so they compare entire strictly commuting mapping-space squares. The endpoint naturality also respects composition: in the triangle spaces $V(a,b,d)$ of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], reversal interchanges the two short edges and reverses the long edge. Hence it interchanges precomposition and postcomposition under the displayed mapping-space comparison; the natural pinch comparisons identify these with the canonical composition classes of that node. The same reversal of maps on parameter simplices commutes with every face and degeneracy, retaining the higher compatibility data. Reversal of the interval interchanges its endpoints and identifies the opposite of the path pullback $P(u,v)$ with $P(v^{\mathrm{op}},u^{\mathrm{op}})$, exchanging the two factors. It preserves the constant-path comparison. Together with reversal-invariance of weak equivalences and [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] along the natural zigzags, this proves that these mapping-space comparisons preserve and reflect the homotopy-pullback tests. The Kan replacement in this paragraph ensures that every application of path-pullback invariance has Kan corners; no Kan condition on a subdivision is asserted.

proof.text: It remains to justify isofibrations after reversal, since their definition specified a source. Let $p:D\to B$ be an isofibration and $v:b\to p(x)$ an equivalence in $B$. Choose an inverse edge $u:p(x)\to b$ and lift it, by source lifting, to an equivalence $\widetilde u:x\to y$ with $p(y)=b$. Choose an inverse $w:y\to x$ in $D$. Its image $p(w)$ and $v$ are both inverses to $u$, so the composition-class assertions of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] put them in the same component of $\operatorname{Map}_B(b,p(x))$, and hence in the same component of $U_B(b,p(x))$ by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. The last assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], valid for any inner fibration, says $U_D(y,x)\to U_B(b,p(x))$ is a Kan fibration of Kan complexes. By [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre], path components of these Kan realizations are their vertices modulo finite edge zigzags. Lift a finite edge zigzag joining $p(w)$ to $v$, starting at $w$; each step uses the appropriate one-dimensional horn lift, so the final vertex $w'$ has endpoints exactly $y,x$ and image exactly $v$. It remains in the component of $w$ in $U_D(y,x)$, hence represents the same invertible mapping class by the pinch comparison and the mapping-composition criterion. Thus $w'$ is an equivalence. This proves target lifting in $D$. Reversal makes this exactly source lifting for $p^{\mathrm{op}}$, which is already an inner fibration by step 6. Therefore $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an isofibration.

source.place: Opposite form of the isofibration equivalence-lifting condition; inverse-edge and Kan-mapping-space calculation; online sources read, archive WANTED; explicit agent argument.

proof.text: Finally take a diagram $q:M^{\triangleleft}\to D$ and any test diagram $t$ on the same left cone. Step 6 identifies their opposite diagrams on $(M^{\mathrm{op}})^{\triangleright}$, and identifies the functor categories and both restriction functors. Step 7 changes the four corners of the $p$-limit testing square, whose mapping spaces have arguments $(t,q)$, into those of the $p^{\mathrm{op}}$-colimit square with arguments $(q^{\mathrm{op}},t^{\mathrm{op}})$. It preserves the path-pullback condition. Reversal is involutive and gives a bijection on all test diagrams, so the quantifier over $t$ is exactly the quantifier needed on the other side. The definitions in [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] therefore give the equivalence of the two universal-diagram predicates for arbitrary $p$ and arbitrary small $M$. Applying (1)-(3), already proved, to the opposite data and reversing back proves all their duals. The hypothesis checks are explicit: inner fibrations and equivalences reverse, initial objects become final objects by the mapping-space comparison, isofibrations reverse by step 8, and the horn definition in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] changes cocartesian horns $\Lambda_0^n$ with edge $01$ into cartesian horns $\Lambda_n^n$ with edge $(n-1)n$. All equalities of prescribed maps survive because reversal is an involution on simplicial maps.
